description: Per-case overrides applied on top of doc/spec/case_inventory.json for the Linux reference DUT (other DUT platforms supply their own overrides file via --inventory-overrides). Four independent axes: (1) `expected:false` (+ `reason`) marks a spec case the harness intentionally cannot cover (e.g. wall-time-permanent-deferred shapes) — counted as a gap by `--vs-spec`; (2) `platform_known_fail:true` (+ `platform_known_fail_ref`) marks a case that fails on this file's target platform due to platform-specific kernel/stack deviations from RFC MUST/SHOULD but passes on a strict-RFC DUT — kept ACTIVE in coverage reports so spec coverage stays honest, and filtered out of CI/smoke skip lists via `--exclude-platform-known-fail`; (3) `timing_serial:true` (+ `timing_serial_ref`) marks a case whose verdict measures a sub-second inter-frame cadence (a strict frame_delta_within_us window) that the reference DUT can only meet when NOT CPU-starved — CI runs these UNCONTENDED (--workers 1) via `--only-serial` and drops them from the parallel lane via `--exclude-serial`, mirroring how a conformance lab measures timing on dedicated DUT hardware; the case stays ACTIVE in coverage; (4) `neg_expected:false` (+ `neg_reason`) marks the case's harness-only `_NEG` self-validation sibling as inapplicable on this DUT WITHOUT deferring the positive base — `--exclude-deferred` drops only the registered case whose id ends in `_NEG`. Needed because a `_NEG` mutation test is meaningful only where the fault can be injected: the §4.2 ARP negatives drive an lwIP egress flavor (UT 0x18 OpSetArpFlavor), inert on the Linux kernel's seam-less ARP path. The base `expected` axis cannot express this (base and `_NEG` share one canonical SpecCase, so deferring it would drop the passing positive too). The axes are disjoint in practice but can coexist on a single entry. Schema v3 renamed the second axis from `linux_known_fail` when the lwIP DUT became the second platform consumer; v4 added the third (timing_serial) axis; v5 added the fourth (neg_expected) axis.

ARP_07.neg_reason: ARP_07_NEG drives the lwIP egress fault (UT 0x18 OpSetArpFlavor / kArpFaultOpcodeWrong). On the Linux reference DUT the kernel emits §4.2 ARP with no firmware seam, so the arm is inert (answered kStatusUnknownOpcode) and the negative would land on fail_compliant. Excludes only the negative; the positive ARP_07 still runs and passes on Linux. Active on dut/lwip_dut/inventory_overrides.json (memory/project_conformance_verdict_model.md)
